tooltips.reportType:
Category of reports involved in this anomaly:
• Garbage - waste collection issues
• Lighting - street light problems
• Tree - tree maintenance needs
• Hazard - safety hazards
• Animal - stray or injured animals
• Maintenance - broken public equipment
• Pest - rodent or insect problems
tooltips.anomalyType:
Type of anomaly detected by the system:

📈 Spike - Sudden increase in report volume (e.g., 15 reports vs. avg 2/day)

🐌 Slow Response - Reports taking longer than usual to resolve

🗺️ Geo Cluster - Multiple reports concentrated in small geographic area
tooltips.severity:
Impact level of the anomaly:

🔴 High - Requires immediate attention
   • Spike: >200% above normal
   • Slow: >2x average resolution time
   • Cluster: High density concentration

🟠 Medium - Should be addressed soon
   • Spike: 100-200% above normal
   • Slow: 1.5-2x average time
   • Cluster: Moderate concentration

🟡 Low - Monitor for changes
   • Spike: 50-100% above normal
   • Slow: 1.2-1.5x average time
   • Cluster: Light concentration
tooltips.reviewStatus:
Indicates whether the anomaly has been reviewed by staff:

✅ Reviewed - Staff acknowledged and are aware

⏳ Mark as Reviewed - Click to mark as seen

Multiple staff members can review the same anomaly.

cityHealth.title: City Health Dashboard
cityHealth.summaryTooltip: Overall health metrics for the city. These KPIs provide a snapshot of current report management status and workload trends.
cityHealth.openReportsTooltip: Total number of reports that are currently unresolved (not yet closed). Lower is better. Trend shows change from previous period.
cityHealth.unresolvedTooltip: Percentage of all reports that remain unresolved. Target: Keep below 30% for optimal efficiency. Green = good, Red = needs improvement.
cityHealth.avgResolutionTooltip: Average number of days it takes to resolve a report. Shows how many % above or below SLA target. Green = good (below SLA), Red = needs improvement (above SLA).
cityHealth.incomingTooltip: Average number of new reports submitted per day. Compared to resolved rate. Green = resolving more than incoming (good), Red = backlog growing.
cityHealth.trendTooltip: Change in open reports compared to previous period. ↑ = increasing workload, ↓ = decreasing workload.
cityHealth.bottlenecksTooltip: Identifies which report categories take longest to resolve. Categories with high avg time and high SLA breach rates are bottlenecks needing attention.
cityHealth.avgResolutionTimeTooltip: Average days from report creation to resolution in this category. Compare across categories to find slow areas.
cityHealth.reportCountTooltip: Total number of reports in this category during the selected time period.
cityHealth.slaBreachRateTooltip: Percentage of reports that exceeded their SLA deadline. High rates indicate service level issues.
cityHealth.statusFlowTooltip: Shows the average time reports spend in each status. Long times in early statuses (Open/Pending) indicate delays in processing.
cityHealth.statusFlowTip: 💡 Tip: The green bar shows what percentage of a reports total lifecycle is spent in each status. Aim for balanced distribution.
cityHealth.agingReportsTooltip: Tracks reports that are aging beyond acceptable timeframes. Reports 30+ days old require immediate escalation. This helps identify long-standing issues.
cityHealth.sevenDaysTooltip: Reports unresolved for 7+ days. These are starting to age.
cityHealth.fourteenDaysTooltip: Reports unresolved for 14+ days. Needs attention soon.
cityHealth.thirtyDaysTooltip: Reports unresolved for 30+ days. Requires immediate escalation and priority handling.
cityHealth.workloadTooltip: Compares incoming reports to resolved reports. If incoming > resolved, backlog grows. Target: Resolve more than incoming.
cityHealth.incomingWorkloadTooltip: New reports submitted per day. High volume increases workload.
cityHealth.resolvedWorkloadTooltip: Reports closed per day. Higher is better. Should ideally exceed incoming rate.
cityHealth.priorityActionsTooltip: AI-generated recommendations based on current dashboard metrics. These are actionable suggestions to improve city health.
cityHealth.allNormal: ✅ All metrics are within normal parameters. Great job!
cityHealth.reportsOlderThan30DaysImmediateActionReq: Reports older than 30 days require immediate action.
cityHealth.highUnresolvedRate: High unresolved report rate detected. Focus on closing more reports.
cityHealth.considerAllocatingMoreResources: Consider allocating more resources to high-bottleneck categories.

statusTransition.title: Status Transition Analysis
statusTransition.description: This view analyzes how long it takes for reports to move from one status to another, based on historical status changes.

instructions.step1: Select Time Range: Choose the period you want to analyze
instructions.step2: Select Category: Filter by report type or choose all categories
instructions.step3: Select From/To Status: Pick the status transition you want to examine (e.g., Open → Pending)
instructions.step4: Click Analyze: View average time for this specific transition
instructions.step5: Optional: Download full report or view heatmap of all transitions

statusTransition.downloadComplete: Download complete analysis for all 6 status transitions
statusTransition.heatmapTooltip: View transition matrix for all statuses
statusTransition.heatmapLegend: Values show average days to transition | Numbers in parentheses show report count
statusTransition.avgTimeToTransition: the average time to transition from

explanations.open_to_pending: Open → Pending transition measures the initial review and decision time for a report. Long times (>3 days) may indicate overload in the administrative team or lack of manpower for reviewing new reports. Useful for identifying issues in the triage phase.
explanations.open_to_in progress: Direct transition from Open to In Progress indicates urgent handling of critical reports without a pending stage. Ideal for emergencies. If this happens frequently for regular reports - the workflow may not be properly implemented.
explanations.open_to_resolved: Direct transition from Open to Resolved is rare and exceptional. May indicate classification errors, duplicate reports closed immediately, or workflow issues. Worth examining if these cases are legitimate.
explanations.pending_to_in progress: Pending → In Progress transition measures the assignment and actual work start time. Long times (>5 days) indicate shortage in field teams or prioritization issues. This is the most important metric for operational efficiency.
explanations.pending_to_resolved: Direct transition from Pending to Resolved may indicate self-resolved issues or status errors. Worth checking if the report was actually handled in the field or just marked as resolved without a team visit.
explanations.in progress_to_resolved: In Progress → Resolved transition measures actual field handling time. Long times (>7 days) indicate technical complications, lack of equipment/materials, or logistical issues. Useful for tracking field work efficiency.
